Certificates

How to read a certificate of analysis

What the lot number, test method, purity figure and retention time mean, and how to match a certificate to the vial in hand.

Read the note →

A certificate of analysis is issued by the testing laboratory for one production lot. Check four things: the lot number matches the vial, the test date is recent, the method is stated (HPLC for purity, mass spectrometry for identity), and the purity figure is a number, not a range. A certificate with no lab name or no method is not a certificate.

Handling

Storing lyophilized peptides

Why compounds ship as freeze‑dried powder, how long a sealed vial is stable, and the storage conditions the certificates assume.

Read the note →

Lyophilized (freeze‑dried) peptides are stable at ambient temperature for the days a shipment takes. On receipt, store sealed vials at −20 °C protected from light; most compounds hold specification for 12 months or longer under those conditions. Stability data for the lot is listed on its certificate.

Categories

How this catalog is organized

Four research areas, defined by the models and pathways in the literature rather than by marketing names.

Read the note →

Tissue and matrix: peptides studied in tendon, muscle, skin and extracellular‑matrix models. Mitochondrial and cellular: compounds examined for mitochondrial membrane, AMPK and redox signaling. Neuropeptides: short peptides studied in rodent brain‑tissue models. Receptor pharmacology: analogs used in receptor‑binding assays. Every entry lists the model and a citation.

What research use only means

Who may purchase, what the attestation covers, and why there is no dosing information anywhere on this site.

Read the note →

Products are sold for in‑vitro laboratory research. They are not for human or animal consumption, application or injection, and are not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease. Purchasers confirm they are 21 or older and qualified researchers, and sign a research‑use agreement before a first order. Because of that, the site carries no dosing, administration or outcome information.

FAQ

Questions.

What does “research use only” mean?

Every product is sold strictly for in‑vitro laboratory research. Products are not for human or veterinary consumption, application, injection or any form of bodily administration, and are not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease. Reality Supps is a chemical supplier, not a compounding pharmacy or outsourcing facility under sections 503A or 503B of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

Who can purchase?

Qualified researchers and research organizations, 21 or older. Checkout requires an attestation and first orders require a signed research‑use agreement on file. Orders or messages indicating another intended use are refused and refunded.

Where are the certificates of analysis?

Every compound panel links to its current lot certificate, and the lot lookup opens the certificate for any lot printed on a vial. Certificates are issued by the testing laboratory and published unedited.

How fast do orders ship?

Orders before 2 PM ET ship the same business day from the United States with tracking.

Something is out of stock. When does it return?

Stock changes with each tested lot. Reality Mastery members receive restock notices first.

Reality Mastery members receive restock notices and member pricing first.
